To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) intrinsic thermotolerance and thermotolerance after heat pretreatment are independent phenomena in human tumour cells; (ii) tolerance to heat and oxidative stress in human tumour lines is associated with cellular sulphydryl content; (iii) the stress protein heme oxygease, induced by heat or oxidative stress, may not necessarily be involved in the tolerance of human tumour cell to heat or to oxidative stress.

1) the heat resistance of human tumour cells is not related to heat shock protein induction; 2) the resistance of human tumours cells to heat is related to the intracellular glutathione concentration; 3) the resistance of tumour cells to heat and oxidative stress is not related to heme oxygenase induction.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heat shock response is an important factor in the resistance to heat but not to other stressors.
the relationship between thermotolerance and oxidative stress is not simple.
heat shock proteins are induced by a variety of stresses, and that this induction is not necessarily related to tolerance to these stresses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the induction of heat-shock proteins is not necessarily associated with the induction or the expression of thermotolerance.

the induction of stress proteins is not a general feature of cells exposed to heat and oxidative stress, and that the induction of heme-oxygenase in response to oxidative stress does not necessarily involve a heat-shock-like mechanism.

heat shock proteins and heme oxygenase are not necessarily associated with thermotolerance and oxidative stress tolerance, and that the mechanisms involved in the induction of stress proteins by oxidative stress are not identical in all cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the induction of heat-shock proteins is not a universal response to heat stress in human tumor cells, and that the induction of these proteins may not necessarily be related to thermotolerance.
the relationship between thermotolerance and oxidative stress is complex, and that it may vary between cell lines.
the induction of stress proteins is not the only factor determining cell survival following stress.
